claims.description: After a snapshot is durably persisted and log compaction completes, a restarted or lagging Raft peer must retain a recoverable representation of the committed FSM state and the history needed for continued replication.

scope.description: Snapshot creation, persistence, compaction, snapshot installation, and recovery for the configured SnapshotStore and LogStore.
assumptions: The configured snapshot store and log store satisfy their interfaces.
Crash and storage-error behavior of concrete stores is not supplied.
excluded: FSM application determinism beyond the supplied FSM interface contract.
Concrete filesystem or database atomicity guarantees.

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: Concrete store durability and recovery semantics are unread.

grounding.derivation: The implementation persists an FSM snapshot, records snapshot metadata, compacts logs, and later sends a snapshot to lagging peers. The documentation states that snapshots permit removal of logs used to reach the captured state and that committed entries may be applied to the FSM.
grounding.applicability: Applicable when snapshotting is enabled, a snapshot is successfully created and persisted, and compaction or lagging-peer recovery is exercised.
unresolved: Whether concrete store implementations make persisted snapshot data and metadata durable together.
Whether recovery reconstructs all state required after the selected compaction point.
alternatives: The selected store may provide stronger atomicity or recovery guarantees than the interfaces express.

claims.description: For every successful takeSnapshot path, log deletion must not remove the only recoverable history or snapshot representation needed to reconstruct the FSM state at or before the compacted index and to continue replication.

scope.description: The successful path from Raft.takeSnapshot through SnapshotSink.Close, last-snapshot publication, compactLogs, and later sendLatestSnapshot.
assumptions: The snapshot metadata index identifies the state represented by the persisted snapshot.
The configured LogStore and SnapshotStore implement the documented interface semantics.
excluded: Failure behavior of concrete stores not included in the supplied materials.
Concurrent snapshot deletion or external store mutation.

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: The source for concrete store Close, List ordering, Open durability, and DeleteRange behavior is missing.
The restart reconstruction path is missing.

grounding.derivation: takeSnapshot calls FSMSnapshot.Persist, closes the sink, updates last-snapshot state, and then compacts through compactLogsWithTrailing. A lagging peer is later recovered through sendLatestSnapshot, which selects and opens a listed snapshot. These producer-consumer dependencies make recoverability across compaction an applicable candidate obligation.
grounding.applicability: Applicable only after successful snapshot persistence and close; not established for error paths or concrete stores whose contracts are unread.
unresolved: Whether sink.Close durably publishes the snapshot before compaction.
Whether List returns a snapshot that Open can still recover after compaction.
Whether the FSM snapshot is semantically complete at snapReq.index.
alternatives: TrailingLogs may preserve sufficient incremental history even if snapshot recovery is unavailable, but this is not established.

claims.description: When a new snapshot attempt fails before successful persistence, a previously usable snapshot must remain available if it is the only recoverable representation needed for restart or follower recovery.

scope.description: Applies to snapshot stores that replace or expose the current snapshot before persistence succeeds, especially InmemSnapshotStore, with a prior valid snapshot and a failed Persist path.
assumptions: The prior snapshot is valid and available before the replacement attempt.
The failed persistence is legal and the store is expected to preserve previously usable recovery state.
excluded: Successful persistence followed by completed compaction.
FileSnapshotStore crash durability beyond the supplied implementation range.

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities
pending: Applicability of this obligation to all SnapshotStore implementations requires the concrete store-selection and recovery configuration.
The restart and follower-consumption paths have not been read.

grounding.derivation: The goal requires a recoverable representation after snapshot/compaction operations. The in-memory implementation replaces the prior snapshot during Create, while the failure path calls Cancel, which is a no-op. This derives a candidate producer/consumer obligation for preserving the prior representation across failed replacement.
grounding.applicability: Applicable when InmemSnapshotStore is configured and a prior snapshot exists before a replacement snapshot fails.
unresolved: Whether the surrounding recovery workflow can legally tolerate loss of the prior snapshot after a failed attempt.

associations.rationale: SnapshotStore and snapshot orchestration define the persisted snapshot and compaction boundary relevant to recoverability.
takeSnapshot and compactLogsWithTrailing implement the deletion boundary.

bindings.description: Requests an FSM snapshot, obtains committed configuration, persists it through SnapshotSink, publishes last-snapshot state, and invokes log compaction.

associations.rationale: This declaration computes the deletion range and invokes LogStore.DeleteRange.

bindings.description: Computes the compacted range from snapshot index, last log index, and configured trailing logs, then deletes that range.

associations.rationale: The interface defines the external snapshot publication, listing, and reopening operations consumed by replication.

bindings.description: External snapshot store contract for create, ordered listing, and reopening persisted snapshots.
pending: Concrete implementation and durability contract are unread.

associations.rationale: This behavior opens the selected snapshot and transmits its metadata and contents to a lagging peer.
Recovery after compaction depends on this consumer being able to open a usable snapshot.

bindings.description: Lists snapshots, opens the most recent one, sends it to a follower, and advances follower replication state on success.
pending: Follower installation and restart recovery behavior are unread.

associations.rationale: SnapshotStore and SnapshotSink define the storage lifecycle used by the recovery guarantee.
The concrete replacement and cancellation behavior grounds the candidate obligation.

bindings.description: Creates and immediately installs a new in-memory snapshot as the latest snapshot before persistence completes.

associations.rationale: The failed replacement path invokes a cancellation operation that leaves the replacement state in place.

bindings.description: Cancellation returns success without restoring or removing the replacement snapshot.

associations.rationale: takeSnapshot orders persistence, close, snapshot metadata update, and log compaction.
The replacement failure scenario is initiated by the takeSnapshot lifecycle.

bindings.description: Requests FSM capture, persists and closes the snapshot sink, then updates stable snapshot state and compacts logs.

relations.rationale: The recoverability goal requires the compaction boundary to preserve a usable recovery representation.

grounding.derivation: The goal's consequence is realized through the successful snapshot-to-compaction-to-recovery path.
grounding.applicability: Applicable to snapshot-enabled recovery and lagging-peer catch-up.

relations.rationale: O1 depends on takeSnapshot establishing the persisted snapshot and the exact index before deletion.

grounding.derivation: The producer behavior is the snapshot persistence and publication sequence preceding compaction.
grounding.applicability: Applicable on the successful takeSnapshot path.
unresolved: Whether Close makes data durable before subsequent deletion.

relations.rationale: O1 depends on a later consumer being able to list and open the retained snapshot for a lagging peer.
pending: Snapshot installation and restart reconstruction are not supplied.

grounding.derivation: sendLatestSnapshot is the observed recovery consumer for a follower whose log is too far behind.
grounding.applicability: Applicable when replication reaches ErrLogNotFound and a snapshot exists.
unresolved: Whether the opened snapshot contains all state required by the consumer.

relations.rationale: G1's recoverability guarantee depends on O2 for the applicable InmemSnapshotStore failed-replacement path: the prior usable snapshot must remain available when replacement persistence fails.

grounding.derivation: The documented snapshot lifecycle requires recoverable FSM state after log compaction and supports restoring state from snapshots. The implementation-specific O2 relation checks preservation of the prior snapshot when a replacement fails.
grounding.applicability: Applies to G1 only for the InmemSnapshotStore configuration and the failed replacement scenario covered by O2; it does not generalize to all SnapshotStore implementations.
unresolved: Restart and follower-consumption paths remain unread.
